trial.title: A Prospective Study of Pembrolizumab Combining Chemotherapy in Advanced NSCLC Patients With EGFR Exon 21 Point Mutation.

endpoints.description: the time length from enrollment to any of the following events: disease progression with first line therapy or death from any cause. Disease progression will be assessed according to RECIST 1.1
the time length from enrollment to any of the following events: disease progression with Osimertinib or death from any cause. Disease progression will be assessed according to RECIST 1.1

endpoints.measure: Incidence of adverse events graded according to National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5.0
endpoints.description: Evaluate adverse events of any cause, treatment-related adverse events, immune-mediated adverse events according to NCI-CTCAE V5.0
Proportion of patients with Complete and Partial Responses to first-line therapy.

Evaluate life quality score according to Karnofsky performance status (KPS). On a scale of 10, higher scores indicate better health. A score of 0 is defined as death, on a 100-point scale, indicating normal physical fitness with no obvious symptoms and signs.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06142617 is a Phase II single-arm study evaluating pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed/platinum as first-line therapy followed by osimertinib at progression in EGFR exon 21 mutation-positive advanced NSCLC patients with PD-L1 TPS≥1%.

Evidence from KEYNOTE-789 (pembrolizumab+chemotherapy in TKI-resistant EGFR-mutant NSCLC) showed no significant PFS/OS benefit vs chemotherapy alone, indicating limited efficacy of immunotherapy in EGFR-mutant populations.
Evidence from CAP29 real-world study (non-EGFR mutant NSCLC) showed median PFS 9.0 months with pembrolizumab+pemetrexed-platinum, ORR 63.7%, and grade 3-4 AEs in 17.5%.

EGFR-mutant NSCLC typically shows lower immunotherapy response due to lower TMB and distinct immune microenvironment; exon 21 L858R may have slightly better ICI response than exon 19del per emerging data.

PFS1 prediction: Based on KEYNOTE-789 negative results in EGFR-mutant population and CAP29 data in unselected NSCLC, median PFS1 likely 4-7 months in this EGFR-mutant population, lower than non-mutant.
PFS2 prediction: Osimertinib after progression on chemo-immunotherapy; historical osimertinib PFS after first-line TKI failure is approximately 10-13 months, but sequence effect unknown.
ORR prediction: Expected lower than non-EGFR mutant due to intrinsic resistance; estimated 30-45% based on EGFR-mutant chemo-immunotherapy data.
Safety: Expected grade 3-4 AE rate ~15-25% based on KEYNOTE-189/CAP29; immune-mediated AEs consistent with pembrolizumab profile.
Quality of life: Expected maintenance or slight improvement during response period, decline at progression; no specific quantitative anchor available.
Key uncertainty: No direct evidence for first-line chemo-immunotherapy specifically in EGFR exon 21 mutation; KEYNOTE-789 was TKI-resistant setting, not treatment-naive.

Evidence role assignments: CAP29 (indirect_direction, numeric_use_allowed=false, mismatch=EGFR status), KEYNOTE-789 (indirect_direction, numeric_use_allowed=false, mismatch=population TKI-resistant vs treatment-naive), KEYNOTE-189 (mechanism_background, mismatch=excluded EGFR mutations).
